title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is written upside down (rotated 180°). It holds sparse scratch notes in blue ink and is crossed by a long pencil diagonal, which in Grothendieck's manuscripts usually means the page was discarded or superseded. It sits between p.57 and p.59.

On p.57 Grothendieck builds a canonical k-linear ('h-lin') category P containing a given category A. P contains a cochain complex C^• and an object Ψ^0 that represents L ↦ Hom(L,C^0)^∨. This makes C^• a Ψ^0-augmented complex. P_0 is the full subcategory of finite sums of objects of the form L⊗(Ψ^0)^r. Σ is the class of sequences that the projective objects P∈P_0 turn into exact sequences, and the augmented complex (C^•,Ψ^0,ε) is a Σ-resolution.

On p.59 he unpacks this into short Σ-exact sequences 0→Ψ^i→C^i→Ψ^{i+1}→0. He shows that on the subcategory generated by the Φ^i and Ψ^j, the functor L ↦ Hom(Φ^•,L) is fully faithful onto finite chain complexes of free modules of finite type. He then states that the k-additive category is universal for an exact structure Σ equipped with a Σ-resolution of an object. Finally he adds axiom (d): pushouts and pullbacks of Σ-exact sequences exist in P, as in a Quillen exact category.

This page is the bridge: a sketch of that universal property. The legible fragments are:
- A struck-out start: 'Hom^•_k(L^•,C^•) → Z^n(C^•), B^n(C^n)', i.e. cocycles and coboundaries of a Hom complex, '...comme un E-...'.
- A small diagram 'Hom_{E-ex} ↓ B' with a branch 'Hom_{E-ex} ≃ B_{?}' (subscript illegible, possibly 'ex' or 'n.e'). This reads as: functors that are exact for the exact structure E, from P into a target B, are equivalent to some category built from B (resolution data or augmented complexes in B).
- A side remark: 'B est abélienne' (B is abelian), then 'M ... (?)' with illegible words, probably the special case of an abelian target.
- 'Ext^1(L^•,M^•) ⟹ 0', probably a vanishing condition needed so that the extension or resolution data are unique.
- The final display 'Hom_{E-ex}(P^•,B) ≃ Hom_{E-ex}(P_0?,B)' with 'B ... E-adjoint ...'. This says exact functors from the full category are determined by their restriction to the generating subcategory, via an adjoint.

The problem served: describe the free or universal k-linear exact category generated by an exact sequence or resolution. This is presumably a step toward 'dévissage' of ∂-perfect half-simplicial complexes and multiplicative (K-theoretic or λ-ring) structures, where one wants functors out of a universal model to classify resolution data in any exact category.
errors: Too fragmentary to verify. The equivalence Hom_{E-ex}(P,B) ≃ (resolution data in B) is only asserted in outline, with no proof. Its validity depends on P_0 generating and on the pushout/pullback axiom (d), which is introduced only on the next page.
The pencil diagonal suggests Grothendieck himself discarded or superseded this sketch.

ideas.what: Universal property: exact functors from the canonically constructed k-linear exact category P into an exact (or abelian) category B correspond to exact functors from the generating subcategory, or to augmented-resolution data in B.
ideas.modern_name: Free / universal exact category on a resolution; 2-universal property of an exact hull
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen's exact categories (1973); universal-property characterisations by Keller, Waldhausen, and later the noncommutative-motives literature (Tabuada)

ideas.what: Vanishing of Ext^1 between complexes as the condition for uniqueness of the resolution data.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity / Ext^1-vanishing for uniqueness of extensions

missed.claim: Sketch of a universal property for the k-linear exact category freely generated by a Σ-resolution (exact functors out of it ≃ resolution data in the target). It feeds the program of p.59, where such a category is called 'universelle'; it is not carried out on this page.
missed.quote: Hom_{E-ex}(P^·, B) ≃ Hom_{E-ex}(𝒫^·, B) ... B est abélienne
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Universal exact or stable categories classifying a resolution or filtration are close to later constructions of free stable ∞-categories and of universal K-theory models. Here it is only a crossed-out fragment, so its value is mainly historical.

deep.surprise_reason: A discarded, nearly illegible scratch page. It hints at a universal property of a constructed exact category, which is standard in spirit and only sketched.
transcription_corrections: The page is upside down; the transcription order should start from the physical bottom ('Si ... q.h.' line, then the struck 'Hom^·_k(L^·,C^·) → Z^n(C^·), B^n(C^n)' line, then 'comme un E-...').
The 'B_{tis}' reading is doubtful; possibly 'B_{ex}' or a similar subscript. 'B_{n.e}' is likely 'B_{ne}' or 'B n.e.'.
In 'Ext^1(L^·, M^·) ⟹ 0', the arrow may be '= 0' with an implication sign.
The second argument in 'Hom_{E-ex}(P^·,B) ≃ Hom_{E-ex}(𝒫^·,B)' may be 'P_0' (the generating subcategory from p.57) rather than '𝒫^·'.
